brief: JPMorgan reframes NVDA's debate ahead of F3Q27 around CEO succession and China export risk rather than fundamentals. A second personal-relationship disclosure this week (after Jensen Huang's own Sunday admission, tied to Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset) adds to an existing board investigation and government probes; NVIDIA's conflict-of-interest code could expose Huang to removal as CEO. Shares fell ~9% after-hours. JPMorgan frames the near-term question as whether the board can install an interim team that preserves execution on the already-set 2-3 year roadmap, and the longer-term question as whether leadership can spot the next computing inflection. Separately, citing heightened national-security risk, JPMorgan removes NVDA's 'China + Other' shipments (~8% of F1H27 revenue) from its FY28 estimates, cutting FY28 EPS ~10% and the price target to $215 (from $320) at ~15x new FY28 EPS. It also flags Southeast Asian intermediary enforcement risk, customer supplier diversification, ASIC/XPU share gains toward parity, and memory-cost margin pressure. Rating stays Overweight.
